advances: One integer coordinate, one genuine globally critical cap, and the original adjacent midpoint row. The own capture condition and global maximum hypothesis are part of the result.

proof:
If both neighboring strict residuals are nonempty, intersect each with a compact stricter-margin cut of the original strict complement. The two sets are nonempty for all sufficiently small margin decrements. Convexity of $C$ and the affine margin imply that their Minkowski midpoint lies in the source strict residual. Brunn–Minkowski for nonempty compact convex sets, including null sets, and continuity from below as the margin decrement tends to zero give the weak midpoint bound.

For an empty neighbor, translate $i$ to zero and reflect the base coordinate if needed so the strict residual at $-1$ is empty. The source residual has positive volume. The projection of the convex set $C\setminus H$ is an interval containing zero. Hence it contains no negative integer base, since otherwise it contains $-1$. This proves the claimed full captures on the negative side, even for null fibers. Write $H=\{u\cdot x+a z\ge b_0\}$. The coefficient $u$ is nonzero since otherwise the containing cap would take the entire source fiber. The tilt $H_L=\{u\cdot x+(a-L)z\ge b_0\}$, $L\ge0$, fixes the source trace, retains the negative fibers, and decreases every positive trace. For a sufficiently large finite $L$ it strictly misses all positive integer fibers by compactness and finiteness. Since $H_L$ still contains the same depth-$Q$ mark, its mass is at least $Q=\mu(H)$, so every positive capture in the original $H$ has zero volume. This proves the step mass identity. Original zero-volume captures may be nonempty.

Normalize $v_0=1$ by scaling the continuous coordinates. Put $b=v_1$. Whenever $b>1$, the actual nonempty $C_{-k}$ satisfies $(C_{-k}+kC_1)/(k+1)\subset C_0$ for integer $k\ge1$, so Brunn–Minkowski gives $v_{-k}\le1-k(b-1)$, including nonempty null $C_{-k}$. Absent fibers have zero mass. Therefore the step identity gives
$$
Q\le p+\sum_{k\ge1}[1-k(b-1)]_+^d,\qquad Q\ge\gamma_d b^d.
$$
For the lower bound use the volume centroid of the positive-volume $C_1$, taking the full-volume selector in fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d. Every containing ambient cap at that centroid either has a containing continuous halfspace trace or includes the whole fiber, and all other contributions are nonnegative. Global maximality of $Q$ gives the comparison.

For $d\ge2$, $1/3<\gamma_d\le4/9$. The first three terms of $(1+1/d)^d$ sum to at least $9/4$, and its whole binomial expansion is bounded above by $\sum_{k\ge0}1/k!<3$, using $k!\ge2^{k-1}$ for $k\ge2$ with strict inequality for $k\ge3$. If $d=2$ and $b\ge\sqrt2$, the upper estimate for $Q$ is at most
$$
\tfrac12+(2-\sqrt2)^2+(3-2\sqrt2)^2=\tfrac{47}2-16\sqrt2<\tfrac89.
$$
The strict comparison follows from $407^2<2\cdot288^2$, while the lower bound gives $Q\ge(4/9)b^2\ge8/9$. If $d\ge3$ and $b\ge3/2$, only $k=1$ can contribute positively and $Q\le1/2+1/8=5/8$, whereas $Q>(3/2)^d/3\ge9/8$. Thus $b<\sqrt2$ for $d=2$ and $b<3/2$ for $d\ge3$. The source has $f_0=(1-p)^{1/d}\ge2^{-1/d}$, where $2^{-1/d}=\sqrt2/2$ when $d=2$ and $2^{-1/d}>3/4$ when $d\ge3$. In either dimension range $f_0>b/2\ge f_1/2$.

If $p\le\gamma_d$ and $b\ge10/7$, the upper bound on left mass is $(4/7)^d+(1/7)^d\le17/49$. Consequently $(100/49)\gamma_d\le Q\le\gamma_d+17/49$, contradicting $\gamma_d>1/3$. Thus $b<10/7$. Since $(1-\gamma_d)^{1/d}\ge\sqrt5/3>5/7$, subtraction yields the strict reserve. Finally reverse the normalization and reflection.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive mixed mass, with $\mu(E)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}|C_j\cap E_j|$. Let $(i,x)$ be a global maximizer of raw closed-halfspace depth $Q$, with $|C_i|>0$. Suppose one closed ambient halfspace $H$ contains $(i,x)$ and has $\mu(H)=Q$. Put $p=|C_i\cap H_i|/|C_i|\le1/2$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $v_j=|C_j|^{1/d}$, and $f_j=|C_j\setminus H_j|^{1/d}$, with zero roots for absent or null fibers. Then
$$
f_i\ge\frac{f_{i-1}+f_{i+1}}2.
$$
If the strict residual at $i-1$ is empty, $C_j\subset H_j$ for every $j<i$, all captures at $j>i$ have zero volume, and $Q=\sum_{j<i}|C_j|+p|C_i|$. The reversed assertion holds for an empty strict residual at $i+1$. In either empty-neighbor case the midpoint comparison is strict. If additionally $p\le\gamma_d$, then
$$
f_i-\frac{f_{i-1}+f_{i+1}}2>
\left(\frac{\sqrt5}{3}-\frac57\right)v_i>0.
$$
title: A low-capture critical cap satisfies nearest-neighbor residual comparison
